title: Relative flatness of explicit strict-perfect tensor terms
statement: Let f:X→S be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], U an open, L a strictly perfect complex on the open site over U [def-pc-perfect-complex], and G a complex of O_X-modules all of whose terms are affine-locally flat over f [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. Each term of the explicit complex T [def-pc-strict-perfect-relative-tensor-complex] is flat as a sheaf of modules over (f inverse-image O_S)|_U [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. There are no derived objects, representative isomorphisms, degree intervals, quasi-coherence or nonempty-open assumptions.

proof.text: Restrict each G term to the open site and restrict scalars along the canonical inverse-image structure ring map. relativeFlat_open_scalarRestriction supplies base-flatness for each restricted term, without quasi-coherence.

Extract the finite free inclusion and retraction for every L term from IsStrictlyPerfect. Apply isFlat_scalarRestricted_tensor_retract to it and each restricted G term. Every scalar-restricted tensor summand is flat. The boundedness clause is unnecessary for termwise flatness.

By the explicit construction, total degree n is the coproduct of summands indexed by integer pairs with sum n. Scalar restriction preserves these coproducts, proved by reflection through the forgetful functor to abelian sheaves. Lift the index type to the module universe, apply isFlat_coproduct, reindex by Equiv.ulift, and transport right-tensor exactness across the resulting canonical coproduct isomorphism. This proves every term flat, including empty and zero cases.
